 Sabres at Stars | How to watch, lineup notes, and storylines
 Alex Lyon is expected to start again in net.
 By 
 Justin Alpert 
 Sabres.com 
 November 14, 2026 
 Link copied 
 DALLAS – The Buffalo Sabres take on the Dallas Stars on Saturday at 8 p.m. EST at American Airlines Center.
 Buffalo (8-7-4) is currently searching for a middle ground between all-out offensive pressure and defensive responsibility. It had the former in Wednesday’s game against Tampa Bay, but it opened rush opportunities for the Lightning’s dangerous forwards and resulted in an 8-3 loss.
 The Sabres then leaned the other direction Thursday in Chicago, tightening up the defense but struggling to find their offensive footing, apart from first-period goals by Owen Power and Tage Thompson. A 3-2 overtime loss – with some controversy at the end – has the Sabres winless in their last three games (0-2-1).
 “There was a lot of good on the defensive side of it,” coach Lindy Ruff said postgame. “I thought we missed some good opportunities to take advantage of some of the O-zone time we had. But if you play defense like that, you’re going to give yourself a chance to win every night.”
 Things won’t get much easier Saturday against the 10-6-2 Stars, who haven’t scored a ton but have been one of the NHL’s stronger defensive teams. That said, Dallas is coming off an 8-3 home loss to Winnipeg, so perhaps the Sabres are in town at the right time.
 Here are all the details before puck drop.
 How to watch 
 TV (Sabres broadcast market): MSG (Pregame coverage begins at 7:30 p.m.)
 Streaming (Sabres broadcast market):  DAZN
 Radio:  WGR 550 /  Buffalo Sabres App 
 More ways to watch/listen to Sabres games 
 Lineup notes (updated 7:35 p.m.) 
 Alex Lyon is expected make a second straight start in net. He returned from injury for his season debut Thursday in Chicago, stopping 22 of 25 shots.
 Based on pregame line rushes, the rest of the lineup will be unchanged from Thursday:
 Notable numbers 
 With 12 goals, Thompson is on pace for 53 this season. Last time Buffalo visited Dallas, Thompson had three points (2+1) in a New Year’s Eve win.
 Two assists in Chicago give Jack Quinn 19 points (9+10) in 19 games. His career high is 51 points (20+31), set last season.
 The Sabres enter Saturday on an eight-game road point streak (4-0-4). Their only road regulation loss came opening night in Columbus.
 Scouting the Stars 
 Goalie Jake Oettinger, who had a 26-save shutout in Buffalo last month, was pulled Thursday after allowing six goals on 27 shots.
 The Stars yielded a season-high-tying 30 shots in the 8-3 loss – they’ve allowed the second-fewest shots per game (23.3) in the league. And per Stathletes, they’ve also allowed the second-fewest high-danger chances per game (1.72).
 Dallas is expected to be without star defenseman Miro Heiskanen due to an upper-body injury, although Heiskanen did participate in Saturday's morning skate. And fellow blueliner Lian Bischel (lower body) will also be unavailable after exiting Thursday’s loss.
